title: introduce-bellcurve-autoscaler-and-utilization-exposure
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets have two recurring failure modes: noisy spikes cause overprovisioning and oscillatory scale-downs hurt long-tail cost. This PR implements a new 'bellcurve autoscaler' algorithm and an exposure-style utilization telemetry signal to make scaling decisions robust to transient outliers while preserving fast upscales for real demand. The bellcurve autoscaler computes a Gaussian-weighted window over recent utilization samples, producing a smoothed utilization estimate that discounts single-sample spikes but still respects sustained increases. We combine that with a stepwise scale policy: small, deterministic up-steps for latency-critical pools and conservative tiered down-steps with a configurable micro-epoch to reduce oscillation. Additionally, the PR introduces a burst-safety limiter that caps ephemeral burst grants relative to the fleet's recent p95 sustained throughput to avoid starving committed tenants. Key config knobs: scale_step_ms (how frequently to allow step changes), decay_sigma_ms (Gaussian sigma for weighting), safety_tail_buffer_pct (percent headroom retained when capping bursts), and micro_epoch_ms (minimum time between scale-downs). Work completed: 1) autoscaler core: pkg/autoscaler/bellcurve_controller.go with public interface compatible with existing ScaleDecider; 2) config and defaults: pkg/autoscaler/config.go and defaults for Dedicated fleets; 3) safety limiter: pkg/autoscaler/burst_safety_limiter.go that audits historical pXX sketches and enforces a soft cap with exponential backoff if bursts exceed threshold; 4) telemetry: telemetry/collectors/util_exposure_collector.go and metrics_registry.go registering new metrics redwood.util.exposure.p50|p95|p99 and redwood.util.exposure.delta; 5) docs and runbook: docs/autoscaling/bellcurve.md describing behavior, tuning guide, and rollback steps; 6) integration and perf: examples/perf-canary/bellcurve_loadgen.yaml and perf-canary harness patch to exercise micro-epochs; 7) tests: unit tests and deterministic e2e in pkg/autoscaler/controller_test.go. Testing and rollout: unit tests cover corner cases (all-zero traffic, sustained ramp, synthetic microbursts). Perf-canary runs showed 12% lower scale cost over a 48h noisy trace with identical p95 latency. Gradual rollout plan: enable feature flag autoscaler.bellcurve.enabled=false by default, stage to a 5% fleet cohort for next release, then 25% and full rollout after 2 rolling windows. Docs and changelog updated. No customer-facing API changes. Related work: follows design proposal in ENG-4782 and integrates feedback from ENG-5124.

release_notes: Introduce bellcurve autoscaler: Gaussian-weighted smoothing with micro-epoch step policy to reduce oscillation; Burst safety limiter: caps ephemeral grants relative to sustained p95 throughput to protect committed tenants; New utilization exposure metrics (redwood.util.exposure.p50|p95|p99 and .delta) for fine-grained fleet telemetry; Feature behind flag autoscaler.bellcurve.enabled and staged rollout.
notes: Performance regressions were profiled and confirmed below 2% CPU overhead in steady state for 8-proc controllers; memory overhead limited to storing 1 minute of samples per pool. Rollback is configuration-only via feature flag.
